observations: body L1-L8: «Abū Ǵa‘far al-Khāzin», «Ibrāhīm ibn Sinān», divided between L1 and L2, «Arzachel», «Ṣā‘id al–Andalusī», «Alpetragius» and «Abū ‘Alī al–Ḥasan» are letter-spaced; the hyphens of «al-Khāzin» and «az-Zarqālī» measure 3.6 and 1.7 pt, the long dashes of «al–Andalusī» and «al–Ḥasan» 4.2 and 5.4 pt. «heg» (L1) is printed without a full stop, and the e of «Saeculo» prints broken.

body L9-L18: the dash after «b)» measures 9.8 pt, the hyphen of «12-13» 3.6 pt. «al–Battānī» (L12) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.4 pt); «al-Battānī» (L14) and «al-Bīrūnī» (L16) have hyphens (2.5 and 2.0 pt), and «204-209» one of 2.4 pt. Al-Battānī's year of «certain Egyptians and Babylonians» is in chapter XXVII, p. 40, l. 28-29 of the translation.

body L21-L30: «Dhū ’l–qarnayn», «al–mawālīd», «al–‘ālam» and «al–Battānī» (L30) have long dashes (5.4, 5.2, 5.4 and 5.2 pt); the dash before «Brevius» measures 9.4 pt. The x (L24) is an italic letter. Appendix E of the translation is on p. 148, as printed («E. p. 148», with a full stop after the E).
body L31-L34: «Hermetis» is letter-spaced; «intricatam-» (L32) ends with the hyphen of the compound intricatamque.
notes_left L1: «al-Khāzinī» has a hyphen (3.5 pt). Abū Ǵa‘far al-Khāzin (tenth century) is the author of the zīǵ aṣ-ṣafā’iḥ (p. 301); al-Khāzinī (twelfth century) wrote the az-Zīǵ as-Sanǵarī.

notes_left L2-L4: «Naṣīr ad-dīn aṭ-Ṭūsī» and «Qāḍī-zādeh» are letter-spaced. The dash of «aṭ-Ṭūsī» measures 4.2 pt, longer than the hyphen of «ad-dīn» (2.6 pt) in the same name; by its length it is a hyphen. A space (3.0 pt) stands after the hyphen of «at- Tadhkirah», as printed. «Qāḍī-zādeh» and «39,v.-40,v.» have hyphens (3.2 pt each).
notes_right L1-L4: «Suter», «Messahalae» and «Albumasaris» are letter-spaced. The closing parenthesis after «Allāh» prints broken, and the ‘ of «Ma‘shar» prints as a raised point.
